evals.prompt: Execute section 1 of the active change
evals.expected_output: The single tasks.md section is done test-first, wrapped in exactly one Conventional Commits commit with its checkboxes ticked, and execution stops without touching other sections.

expectations.text: A failing test is written before the implementation for each task in the section

check.rubric: Red-before-green ordering per task: a failing test must be authored and observed to fail before its implementation. Ordering is a process property read from the transcript, not decidable from final state.

expectations.text: Exactly one commit is created for the whole section
The commit subject follows Conventional Commits (type(scope): imperative)
The tasks.md checkboxes for this section are ticked and included in that same commit
No task from any other numbered section is implemented

The full quality gate (`make check`, which covers tests beyond this section's own) is run once after all the section's tasks, not per task; the Red phase is confirmed with only the section-relevant test rather than the whole-suite gate

check.rubric: The whole-suite gate (`make check`) must run once after the section's tasks, while the per-task Red confirmation uses only the section-relevant test. This is an ordering/granularity property of the run, read from the transcript.

evals.prompt: Execute section 1 of the active change
evals.expected_output: With two active change directories present, execution stops and asks which change to operate on, modifying nothing.

expectations.text: Execution stops and asks the user which change to operate on

check.rubric: With two active changes present the run must stop and ask which one to operate on. 'Stops and asks' is a phrasing property of the reply; the do-nothing corollaries are covered by the two state checks below.

expectations.text: No source or spec files are modified
Change directories under archive/ are excluded from the ambiguity

check.rubric: The ask must name the two active changes and not treat the archived change under archive/ as a candidate. Requires reading which changes the reply enumerates.

evals.prompt: Execute section 1 of the active change
evals.expected_output: A section annotated for delegation is dispatched as a complete spec rather than being reasoned out inline: to the named leaf agent when its role is installed, or, in a rosterless harness where that role is not installed, to a general subagent carrying the role's one-line contract with the report noting the role in fallback form (such as `sai-hu (fallback: general)`).

expectations.text: The dispatch annotation on the section is read and honored
The section is handed to the named agent role as a complete spec

check.rubric: The section must be handed off as a self-contained spec (goal, scope, done-criteria), not reasoned out inline: to the sai-hu role when it is installed, or, in a rosterless harness where that role type is not installed and the dispatch would fail, to a fresh general subagent carrying the sai-hu one-line contract with the report noting the role in fallback form (`sai-hu (fallback: general)`). Either way the handoff must be a complete spec rather than inline reasoning, and a bare without_skill arm produces neither a role dispatch nor a fallback annotation, so the assertion still discriminates. Completeness of the handed-off spec is a quality judgment on the dispatch prompt.

expectations.text: The result is still one Conventional Commits commit with checkboxes ticked
Execution stops after the one section
